Issue_Reported: 1.8 ml of blood for immunology testing was overdrawn with combined blood draw. The deviation occurred when the FARU nurse acquired a second 2 ml blood draw after recognizing the first blood draw was filled less than the 2 ml marker line.
Disposition_Comments: The blood was drawn at 06:30 on this day by FARU nursing and transferred to nutrition personnel. The nutrition personnel reported that the 2 mL Li Hep tube for immunology was filled slightly below the line but did not request a redraw. The nurse drew another 2 ml Li Hep tube. Immune function assessments were completed successfully. The subject was notified. This overdraw was not deemed to be one that would affect the safety of the subject or the integrity of the data. Operations Lead, Project Science, Subject Matter Expert (SME), and Nursing will arrange for a discussion to examine processes involving blood volumes, contacts, stick policies, the proper way to proceed before any more blood is drawn, and a general overview of the tubes used in the combined blood draws. Further training may be required.

Issue_Reported: Urine was not processed immediately after subject voided. Urine was covered from time of void, 10:06, until processing, ~34 minutes later.
Incomplete collection of samples during Tilt test.
Description_of_Action_Taken: CRF completed by test operator indicated incomplete sample collection. Comments: subject hematocrit was higher than expected. There was not sufficient plasma volume for Tilt ANP sample. Per cardiovascular team at the FARU on 6/3, ANP is Atrio Naturietic Peptide. Per blood volume requirements, total blood volume of 83.5 ml for test was collected. Nursing was notified at hand off of subject back to FARU staff. Coordinator on Duty (COD) notified by nursing. COD on 6/3 review of 6/2 CRFs discovered discrepancy and reported to Ops Lead, Study Lead (SL), and backup SL. COD reported to Project Science and entered issues report. Inadequate plasma in blood sample compared to solids after processing is believed by nursing to be the cause of inadequate sample availability.

Issue_Reported: Saliva samples were collected from two subjects this morning, 6858 and 9485, however, both samples were labeled with subject number 6858.
Description_of_Action_Taken: Nursing was able to distinguish one from the other based on a color code, colored dot applied to collection device. This is a documented nursing urine processing practice based upon "Lifewings" practices for accuracy in sample identification. Red dot actually belonged to 9485 and Brown dot to 6858. All parties notified.
Disposition_Comments: No impact to science or otherwise resulted once the samples were identified. The practice of color coding is a secondary measure (backup) for sample identification employed by FARU nursing. In light of this issue, the question has been asked if saliva tubes should be pre-labeled to include the Bed Rest day and the subject number. The lab (Satish) does not object in principle but suggests that labeling may lead to more confusion having to keep track of all pre-labeled tubes as well as delivering those tubes back and forth for every subject included in the study. The problem of mislabeling is rare, but the potential for impact is high. Further work and a final decision is required.

Issue_Reported: The BR 57, saliva sample was delivered to the wrong lab and, as a result, the samples were not properly stored for future processing.
Description_of_Action_Taken: The correct lab was identified, however, 24 hours had elapsed. The sample conditions were reported to affected lab and science impacts were assessed.
Disposition_Comments: Samples at room temperature for 24 hours were no longer acceptable for analysis. The error was not caught in time and action was not taken in time to reschedule sample collection. A Corrective Action was generated to identify the cause of the problem and to define preventive measures. It was determined that the sample loss stemmed from a failure to adhere to established FAP procedures for sample transport and delivery. The change in delivery location for Microbiology samples was not adequately communicated and established procedures did not have sufficient check points or verification steps to transfer the custody of samples to laboratory personnel without error. The corrective action has identified further steps to identify gaps and improve delivery and accountability procedures.
